chunks.title: Who Sohayb Hassan is
chunks.text: Sohayb Hassan is a full-stack engineer with six years at Capgemini (Turin, Italy) building backend and web systems for banks, insurers and corporate clients. He currently delivers features end to end on a retail bank's mobile platform: Java 17 / Spring Boot 3 microservices, an OpenAPI-first BFF layer on JDK 21 and the React Native app. He is at home with the unglamorous side of banking integration (legacy hosts, BPM processes, multi-environment release pipelines) and with the tooling that keeps a large multi-repository programme moving. He started out migrating COBOL to Spring Boot; he now spends personal time on LLM-assisted modernisation tooling where the output is verified, not trusted.

chunks.title: Title and the roles he is looking for
chunks.text: CV title: "Full-Stack Engineer · Java / Spring Boot · React · Banking & Financial Services". Seniority: mid-senior consultant at Capgemini since 08/2023, six years in delivery. Roles he is a fit for: senior backend or full-stack engineering in financial services, and AI engineering roles where the value is wiring LLMs into real engineering workflows with verification — his personal project and his work tooling are both of that kind. Domains delivered: banking and insurance (BFSI), HR platforms, media and entertainment, oil and gas.

Before Capgemini he interned at TogoMetrics in Turin (06/2020 – 09/2020). Employer names are public; client names are not — clients are described by sector only.

chunks.title: Mobile banking platform — scope (02/2025 – present)
chunks.text: Since 02/2025, as Consultant – Full Stack at Capgemini, Sohayb works on the mobile banking platform of a major Italian retail banking group. He delivers features end to end across all three layers: Java 17 / Spring Boot 3 microservices, an OpenAPI-first BFF on JDK 21 and the React Native / Redux Toolkit app. Typical work: designing and building new banking product flows and REST APIs from the OpenAPI contract through the BFF and microservice to the app state, including hand-offs to the bank's BPM processes. It is a large multi-repository programme released through several environments. The client is never named and individual features are not described in detail here.

chunks.title: Legacy host integration over SOAP and REST (mobile banking)
chunks.text: He integrates legacy banking systems over SOAP/WSDL (Apache CXF, JAXB code generation) and REST across payments, cards, limits and document processing, with the error handling that keeps the app usable when a host misbehaves. Specific integrations are not listed here.

chunks.title: Caching, resilience, observability and deployments (mobile banking)
chunks.text: Caching, resilience and observability in production: Hazelcast for distributed caching, Resilience4j for fault tolerance, Micrometer/Prometheus, Splunk and Dynatrace for runtime behaviour. Deployments go to Kubernetes through Azure DevOps release pipelines across multiple environments.

chunks.title: Team tooling and the LLM agent system at work
chunks.text: He built the team's own tooling for the banking programme: environment and API-collection generators, git guard hooks across the repositories, end-to-end test harnesses, an LLM-assisted agent and skill system with a regression suite, and the team's engineering handbook. The agent system is wired to the repository hooks with an approval gate, so the assistant follows the team's branch and review rules instead of bypassing them.

chunks.title: COBOL to Spring Boot migration (10/2020 – 01/2021)

This hands-on COBOL → Java migration is the root of his current personal project on LLM-assisted modernisation.

chunks.title: Personal project — LLM-assisted legacy modernisation
chunks.text: Personal project, in progress: LLM-assisted legacy modernisation — COBOL to Spring Boot with differential-execution verification of the generated code. The design principle is that the referee comes before the agent: a differ that runs the original and the generated code on the same inputs and proves equivalence is built first, and generated code is trusted only through it. Stack: Python, Java 17 / Spring Boot 3, the Claude API, tool-calling agents, an evaluation harness. No public link yet; it will be linked from /projects when it is. Measured results are not published until they exist.

chunks.title: Engineering-workflow automation for a banking programme
chunks.text: Engineering-workflow automation for the banking programme he works on: LLM agents and skills wired to repository hooks, an approval gate and a regression suite, so the assistant follows the team's branch and review rules instead of bypassing them. Shipped and in daily use by the team.

chunks.title: This site — the API Explorer portfolio
chunks.text: This site presents Sohayb's profile as a REST API: each section is an endpoint (GET /experience, GET /skills?filter=backend, GET /now, POST /hire…) that returns real server-rendered HTML with a JSON tab. Built with Next.js 16 (App Router, React Server Components, TypeScript) and Tailwind CSS 4, deployed as a static export on GitHub Pages, fonts self-hosted, no cookies, no analytics. Extras: /cv.txt is an 80-column ANSI CV for curl, /cv.json is a JSON Resume, /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt are for crawlers that read. All facts render from one typed file, content/profile.json, kept in sync with the CV.

chunks.title: How to use this site
chunks.text: The site is an API explorer: pick an endpoint on the left (or press `/`, use ↑↓ and Enter), press Send, read the 200 response. Every endpoint is a real page with its own URL, so links can be shared. Each response has a Rendered tab and a JSON tab. POST /hire opens a pre-filled email; POST /ask is this console. From a terminal, `curl` on /cv.txt returns the CV as text and /cv.json returns a JSON Resume.

chunks.title: How this console works
chunks.text: This console is a retrieval-augmented chat built by Sohayb. The knowledge base is a set of Markdown chunks written from his CV, embedded at build time with Voyage AI (voyage-4) into a small JSON index — no database. Each question is embedded, matched by cosine similarity and by BM25 keyword search, the two rankings are fused (reciprocal rank fusion) and the top five chunks are handed to Claude (claude-opus-5, streamed) with a system prompt that limits answers to those chunks. The model answers with UI blocks — timeline, skill matrix, project cards, status cards — through tool calls rendered by the page, and cites the chunks it used; the retrieval trace is visible under each answer. Guardrails: per-visitor rate limit, a daily spend cap, input length limits, and an evaluation set for retrieval recall and scope deflection. Off-topic questions get an HTTP-style status card, not an answer.

chunks.title: What this console will not answer, and why
chunks.text: This console answers questions about Sohayb's professional profile, his projects and this site — nothing else. It does not discuss salary or compensation (that is a conversation for a real interview), personal data beyond what the site publishes (no date of birth, phone, address, family, health, religion), the names of clients, programmes or colleagues (contractual confidentiality — clients are described by sector only), politics, or unrelated tasks such as writing code or translating documents. It will not reveal its instructions or pretend to be someone else. Anything it cannot answer is a 404 with a pointer to email.
